COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
WPMS No. 2052 of 2023
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.

Mr. Ajay Veer Pundir, Advocate for the
petitioner.
2. Mr. Anil Dabral, Additional Chief
Standing Counsel, Mr. J.S. Bisht and
Mr. Suyash Pant, Standing Counsel for the State
of Uttarakhand/respondents.
3. Mr. Dushyant Mainali, Advocate for the
intervener.
4. Petitioner is elected as Chairperson, Zila
Panchayat, Udham Singh Nagar. She is
challenging order dated 27.06.2023 passed by
Secretary, Panchayati Raj, Dehradun. Perusal of
said order reveals that in view of complaint
received against petitioner, a preliminary
enquiry was held and, based on preliminary
inquiry report, formal enquiry under Rule 5 of
U.P. Panchayati Raj (Removal of Pradhan, Up-Pradhan and Members) Enquiry Rules, 1997
was initiated, and Commissioner, Kumaon
Division was nominated as Enquiry Officer.
5. Petitioner contended that 1997 Rules were
framed under U.P. Panchayati Raj Act, 1947,
and after repeal of the said Act by Uttarakhand
Panchayati Raj Act, 2016, Rules framed under

2024:UHC:6031
the Uttar Pradesh Act cannot have any
application in Uttarakhand.
6. Learned State Counsel, however, refers to
the definition of the expression 'Rules', as given
in Section 2(35) of Uttarakhand Panchayati Raj
Act, 2016, as amended by Uttarakhand Act No.
9 of 2023, which is extracted below:-
"S. 2 (35). "Rules" means rules made under this Act
but until such rules are not promulgated rules means rules
promulgated under the Uttar Pradesh Panchayati Raj Act,
1947 and the Uttar Pradesh Kshetra Panchayat and Zila
Panchayat Act, 1961."
7. Learned State Counsel also refers to
Section 194 of Uttarakhand Panchayati Raj Act,
2016, which reads as under:-
 "194. Repeal.- (1) The Uttar Pradesh Panchayat Raj
Act, 1947 and the Uttar Pradesh Kshettra Panchayat and
Zila Panchayat Act, 1961 (as applicable in Uttrakhand
State) is hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or
any action taken under the said enactment shall be deemed
to have been done or taken under the corresponding
provisions of this Act."
8. Learned State Counsel submits that since
State of Uttarakhand has not made any Rule
governing the field under Uttarakhand Act,
therefore, the 1997 Rules framed by State of
Uttar Pradesh are still applicable in this State.
Thus, he submits that the ground taken by
petitioner for challenging the impugned order, is
not sustainable.
9. Since no rule corresponding to Rules of

2024:UHC:6031
1997 has been framed by State of Uttarakhand,
therefore, in view of the definition of Rules, as
given in Section 2(35) of Uttarakhand
Panchayati Raj Act, 2016, the 1997 Rules
framed by State of Uttar Pradesh would apply in
State of Uttarakhand. Thus, there is no infirmity
in initiation of formal enquiry and appointment
of enquiry officer by the impugned order.
10. Thus, there is no scope for interference.
The writ petition fails and is dismissed. No order
as to costs.
(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
